issues.t: Plastic cooling parts crack and the engine overheats
issues.sym: Low coolant warning, a sweet coolant smell, drips under the front of the car, or the temperature gauge climbing toward hot.
issues.why: The radiator end tanks, expansion tank, thermostat housing, hoses and water pump on these cars use a lot of plastic. Years of heat cycles make it brittle until it cracks or a fitting snaps.
issues.next: Stop driving if the gauge climbs, because overheating can warp the aluminum cylinder head. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and replace the aged plastic parts as a set rather than one at a time.

issues.t: Electric water pump fails and the engine overheats
issues.sym: An engine temperature warning, the cooling fan running at full speed, reduced power, or a check engine light, often with no warning signs beforehand.
issues.why: These engines use an electronically driven water pump, and its motor or electronics can quit, sometimes as early as 50,000 miles. The thermostat often fails along with it.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if the temperature warning appears. A scan tool will usually show a coolant pump fault. Replacing the pump and thermostat together is the normal fix.

issues.t: Worn valve stem seals make the V8 burn oil
issues.sym: Blue-gray smoke from the exhaust right after startup or after idling, frequent low-oil warnings, and oily spark plugs.
issues.why: The rubber valve stem seals on the V8 harden and shrink with heat and age, letting oil run down the valve guides into the cylinders.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and keep it topped up. If the car needs more than about a quart every 1,000 miles, get a quote for valve stem seals from an independent BMW specialist.

issues.t: Twin-turbo V8 burns oil and drains the battery
issues.sym: You add a quart of oil every 1,000 to 2,000 miles, see blue smoke at startup, smell coolant, or keep getting dead batteries.
issues.why: The 550i's turbos sit inside the V of the engine and run very hot. That heat wears valve stem seals and other rubber parts, and the extra electrical load from cooling equipment strains the battery.
issues.next: Track oil use and ask a BMW dealer to check your VIN for work done under BMW's N63 Customer Care Package or the class-action settlement. Change the oil more often than the dash reminder suggests.

issues.t: Timing chain guides break on the 2.0L turbo
issues.sym: A whine that rises with engine speed, a rattle at cold start, timing or camshaft fault codes, or sudden loss of power or stalling.
issues.why: Early versions of this four-cylinder used plastic timing chain guides that became brittle and broke, letting the chain loosen, skip or snap. BMW updated the parts for later builds.
issues.next: Do not ignore a new whine or rattle. A chain that skips can wreck the engine, so have the chain and guides inspected and replaced with updated parts if needed.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump fails and the engine stalls or loses power
issues.sym: Long cranking before the engine starts, stalling soon after starting, a drivetrain malfunction message, hesitation under load, or limp mode.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pump on the twin-turbo 535i failed at a high rate. The first year of the newer single-turbo engine used a similar pump; BMW changed the design for 2012.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the fault codes read to confirm low fuel pressure. Ask a dealer whether any updated pump or software was already installed on your car.
issues.eng: 3.0L twin-turbo inline-6 (535i, N54) / 3.0L turbo inline-6 (535i, N55)

issues.t: Drive belt shreds and can be pulled into the engine
issues.sym: A squeal when revving, a belt that looks frayed, or sudden loss of power steering and charging after a loud slap from the engine bay.
issues.why: Oil leaking onto the belt, worn tensioners or pulleys, and loose pulley bolts can make the belt fray. A broken piece can get sucked behind the crank pulley and into the engine, causing major damage.
issues.next: Fix oil leaks promptly and have the belt, tensioner and pulleys checked at every service. Replace a belt that shows any cracking or fraying right away.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts harshly or slips
issues.sym: Delayed or harsh shifts, slipping, shudder, a transmission warning, being stuck in one gear, or trouble shifting out of Park.
issues.why: The 6-speed automatic's mechatronic unit (the valve body and electronics that control shifting) and its sealing sleeve can fail between about 50,000 and 100,000 miles. BMW called the fluid lifetime, which doesn't help.
issues.next: Have codes read and the fluid level checked. A mechatronic repair or sleeve replacement from an independent specialist can often avoid a new transmission.

issues.t: Older automatic wears out when the fluid is never changed
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed gear changes, shudder at light throttle, a transmission warning light, or limp mode.
issues.why: BMW sold these automatics with 'lifetime' fluid. Many were never serviced, and old fluid speeds up internal wear.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and condition checked. A fluid and filter change every 50,000 to 60,000 miles helps if the transmission is still healthy; a slipping one needs a specialist diagnosis.

issues.t: VANOS valve timing seals wear and power drops
issues.sym: Weak pull at low engine speed, rough idle, hesitation, worse fuel economy, or a rattle from the front of the engine.
issues.why: The variable valve timing (VANOS) unit uses rubber seals that harden and leak with age, usually between 70,000 and 100,000 miles, so the cam timing can't adjust properly.
issues.next: Have a BMW specialist test the VANOS. Rebuild kits with improved seals usually restore the lost power.

issues.t: Valve cover and oil filter housing gaskets leak oil
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning-oil smell after driving, oil in the spark plug wells, or misfires.
issues.why: The rubber gaskets on the valve cover, oil filter housing and oil pan harden with heat and start to seep. Oil dripping onto the exhaust or the drive belt causes smells and damage.
issues.next: Have the source pinned down and replace the gasket. Don't let it run, because oil on the belt can lead to belt failure.

issues.t: Valve cover leaks oil on the 6-cylinder
issues.sym: A burning-oil smell, oil seeping at the back of the engine, or smoke from under the hood after a drive.
issues.why: The valve cover gasket on the 540i's turbo 6-cylinder often starts to leak after about 50,000 miles. Oil can drip onto hot exhaust parts.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the gasket replaced. It is labor-heavy but not urgent unless oil is reaching the exhaust.

issues.t: Oil filter housing cracks and leaks on the 2.0L turbo
issues.sym: Oil or coolant spots under the car, a low coolant warning, or a burning smell.
issues.why: The plastic oil filter housing on this four-cylinder can crack, often between 50,000 and 100,000 miles. It sits under the intake manifold, which makes it hard to reach.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Check the oil and coolant for signs of mixing. Replaced housings rarely fail again.

issues.t: Front thrust arm bushings wear and the wheel shimmies when braking
issues.sym: Steering wheel shake when braking from highway speed, a loose or wandering feel, or clunks over bumps.
issues.why: The fluid-filled rubber bushings in the front thrust arms wear out, often around 75,000 miles and sometimes as early as 40,000.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. New bushings or arms usually cure the shimmy; an alignment afterward is needed.

issues.t: Power window regulator breaks
issues.sym: A window that won't go up or down, moves crooked, or drops into the door with a grinding or clicking noise.
issues.why: The window regulators wear out with age and mileage, front and rear.
issues.next: Keep the window closed and covered if it's stuck open. Replacing the regulator fixes it.

issues.t: Aftermarket steering center rod can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A loose or clunking steering feel could be an early sign.
issues.why: Certain replacement steering center rods made by ZF/Lemförder for this generation had ball joints that could pull out of the steering knuckle, causing a sudden loss of steering.
issues.next: If your steering linkage has ever been replaced, have a shop check the part numbers against the recall and replace an affected rod for free.

issues.t: Sport steering wheel airbag can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. An inflator can explode in a crash and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: Driver airbag inflators in the optional sport steering wheel can degrade with heat and humidity and rupture when they deploy.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov right away. BMW replaces the airbag free, and you should not drive the car until it's fixed if the recall is open.

issues.t: Turbo wastegate rattle on the 535i
issues.sym: A metallic rattle from the turbos, especially when coasting or at light throttle, sometimes with boost-related codes or less power.
issues.why: The linkage bushings in the turbochargers' wastegates wear, letting the flap rattle and eventually fail to control boost.
issues.next: Have a BMW specialist confirm where the rattle is coming from. Mild rattles can be monitored; power loss or codes mean the turbos need repair or replacement.

issues.t: Battery cable connector in the trunk can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Electrical faults, a burning smell from the trunk, or in rare cases a fire even when parked.
issues.why: The positive battery cable's connector on the trunk floor may be poorly attached, so the bolt loosens and the joint heats up.
issues.next: Have the recall checked with your VIN. Until it's done, park outside, away from buildings.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor mat can crack and turn the airbag off (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, or the passenger airbag OFF light stays lit with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The sensor mat in the front passenger seat cracks from people getting in and out, and the system then switches off the passenger airbag.
issues.next: Have a BMW dealer check the recalls on your VIN. The mat is replaced for free.

issues.t: Crankcase vent valve heater can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Sometimes a burning-plastic smell or a check engine light for the crankcase vent heater.
issues.why: A small heater in the crankcase ventilation valve can short circuit and overheat, even with the car parked and off.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have the recall done at a BMW dealer. Until then, park outside and away from buildings if possible.

issues.t: Turbo cooling pump circuit board can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell after shutting the engine off, or coolant or overheating warnings.
issues.why: The electric auxiliary water pump that cools the V8's turbos can fail and overheat its circuit board, which can smolder or catch fire.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN. The pump is replaced for free under the recall.

issues.t: Fuel pump wiring in the tank can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Stalling, hard starting, or a fuel smell.
issues.why: Wire contacts inside the in-tank fuel pump may not be crimped well enough. The connector can melt, leaking fuel or cutting power to the pump.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the recall checked with your VIN. A dealer will install the fix for free.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump can fail and the pedal gets hard (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal, longer stopping distances, or a brake warning message.
issues.why: The engine-driven vacuum pump that powers the brake booster may not get enough oil and can fail, reducing power braking.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. A hard brake pedal means the brake assist has failed, so the car needs much more force and distance to stop. If it happens while driving, press the pedal firmly, slow down and pull off the road when it's safe. Don't keep driving it: have it towed to a dealer. Have a BMW dealer confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Water pump connector can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Sometimes a coolant pump or overheating message, or a burning smell.
issues.why: The electrical connector on the electric water pump may not be sealed well. Water can get in and short it, which can cause a fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have the recall checked with your VIN, and park outside and away from structures until it's done.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag inflators can be damaged by humidity (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. The curtain airbags may not inflate properly in a crash.
issues.why: Long exposure to high humidity can affect the head airbag inflators, and the igniter may separate from the inflator.
issues.next: Have a BMW dealer check your VIN and replace the airbags for free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image can go missing (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the camera picture doesn't appear, the screen stays dark, or part of the image is blocked.
issues.why: Software and settings problems can stop the backup camera image from showing, which breaks federal rear-visibility rules.
issues.next: Use mirrors and look over your shoulder. A dealer software update fixes it for free.

issues.t: Rear axle shafts can break on xDrive models (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear followed by loss of drive, or the car rolling when parked in Park without the parking brake.
issues.why: A supplier heat-treatment error left some rear output shafts weak enough to break.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the recall is checked. A dealer replaces affected shafts for free.

issues.t: Starter relay can corrode and short out (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Possibly a burning smell or a no-start.
issues.why: The starter relay can corrode, overheat and short circuit, which raises the risk of a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and park outside, away from buildings, until it's repaired.

issues.t: Starter can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Slow or failed starts, a burning smell, or smoke from the engine bay after starting attempts.
issues.why: Wear on a part inside the starter can make it overheat, especially with repeated start attempts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Avoid repeated cranking if the engine won't start. Check your VIN for recalls 26V-056 and 26V-438 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Front control arm bushings wear and clunk
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, a vague or wandering steering feel, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front lower control arms wear early, especially on cars driven in rough city conditions.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked. Arms or bushings are usually replaced in pairs, followed by an alignment.

issues.t: Integrated brake unit can lose power assist and ABS (recall)
issues.sym: A brake or stability warning light, a hard pedal, longer stops, or the car behaving unsteadily under hard braking.
issues.why: Welds or electronics inside the integrated braking system (which combines the booster and ABS) can fail, cutting power assist and stability control.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. If a brake warning appears or the pedal goes hard, slow down, pull off the road when it's safe and have it towed to a dealer. Check your VIN; there have been several rounds of this recall.

issues.t: Hands-on steering wheel sensor can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Driver-assist features may not detect your hands on the wheel, and the emergency stop assistant may not step in when it should.
issues.why: A loose ground connection in the steering wheel can disable hands-on detection.
issues.next: Keep your hands on the wheel when using driver assists and have the free recall repair done.

issues.t: Airbag control unit may be built wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Possibly an airbag warning light; often no sign at all.
issues.why: Some airbag control units were not made correctly, so the airbags may not deploy as designed in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN and have the control unit replaced for free.

issues.t: Starter-generator battery cable can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can stall while driving, or warning lights for the electrical system appear.
issues.why: The connection between the starter-generator and the battery may loosen, which can stall the engine and overheat the wiring.
issues.next: Have the recall done promptly. If the engine stalls, steer to a safe place; steering and brakes get heavier without the engine running.
